event.label: Still listed in 1940, the last directory transcribed so far

body.p: Cumberland Place is a short street between the east side of Bouverie Street and the south side of Lincoln Square.

It is first listed in the directories in 1873. It is missing from the 1874 to 1878 directories, and then listed in every directory up to 1940, the last one transcribed so far. It had the most listings, around twenty-five, in the 1890s and 1900s.

div.head: Along the street
div.p: Its two ends are Bouverie Street and the street along the south side of Lincoln Square. The directories list its corner with Bouverie Street from 1900, and its corner with the square from 1915.

div.head: Businesses and landmarks

list.item: A depot of the Albion Motor Car Co. of Australasia Ltd (1925).
The Triumph Battery Co., battery manufacturers (1930 to 1940).

div.p: In 1920 one house, No. 28, is listed only as "Chinese".
